shouldFix.subjectEvidence: A full flatten-and-diff of v5 against v6 yields 87 changed leaf paths, of which exactly two are off-roster: /reMeasurementAtV5/note, rewritten from 'This is the only this-generation live COORD claim. Does not SATISFY DR-121. Does not QUALIFY G16.' to 'HISTORICAL v5 remasurement. Live digest is only at reMeasurementAtV6.', and /reMeasurementAtV5/standing, newly added as 'HISTORICAL-AT-V5'. The declared roster names /reMeasurementAtV6 and nothing else in that family. v5's own roster, by contrast, named /reMeasurementAtV3, /reMeasurementAtV4 AND /reMeasurementAtV5 explicitly - that enumeration was the repair for CLAUDE-V4-S1, and it is exactly what v6 dropped.
shouldFix.impact: Two readings, and both are defects. If the method's catch-all - 'Every path neither the roster nor succession metadata names is unchanged from v5' - is read as exempting re-measurement blocks because they are succession metadata, then the catch-all licenses silent edits to precisely the class of node the roster was widened at v5 to cover, and the closed-roster check stops being a check for that class. If it is read narrowly, the two paths are simply off-roster and this is the silent v5-to-v6 path the artifact's own reviewGuidance instructs a reviewer to attack. The content is benign - relabelling a superseded measurement as historical is correct and this reviewer independently verified the digests it carries - so the discipline is broken rather than the contract.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: Name /reMeasurementAtV5 on the roster, and adopt the standing rule that every generation's roster names the previous generation's re-measurement block, since relabelling it is a predictable consequence of adding a new one. Alternatively tighten the catch-all to enumerate what 'succession metadata' covers, so the exemption cannot silently widen.

systemicObservation: This is the first cycle in this chain with no blocker. Both remaining findings are in the same narrow area - the bookkeeping around re-measurement blocks - and both have the same root cause, which is worth stating plainly because it has now cost a finding in four consecutive cycles: liveness of the coordinator pin is expressed as prose duplicated across six clauses, so every new generation must edit all six, and the roster is sized to the clauses a reviewer named rather than to all six. The structural fix is available and small. Each re-measurement block already carries a 'standing' field; make one of them LIVE and the rest HISTORICAL-AT-V<n>, and have every other clause refer to 'the block whose standing is LIVE' instead of naming a generation. That turns a six-clause edit into a one-field edit, makes the roster question moot for this family, and would have prevented both V6-S1 and V6-S2. The substantive contract - selector, ownership record, lane universe, evidence bindings, G16 classes - is now in good shape: fourteen measurements pass, every Claude v5 finding is discharged at every level it was raised, and both frozen Codex verdicts are characterized exactly.
verdictBasis: Zero blockers and two SHOULD-FIX findings; the dispatch admits ACCEPT only at zero and zero. All six claimed repairs are real and verified against the subject's bytes, and because both frozen Codex verdicts were permitted inputs this reviewer could also verify the predecessor characterizations directly - both are exact. The two surviving findings are confined to re-measurement bookkeeping and neither touches the selector, the evidence contract, or the acceptance classes.
verdictStatement: v6 discharges every finding this reviewer raised at v5, and does so at each level the defect existed rather than at the one clause named. The multi-component predicate is now in the authority enumeration, the closed authority roster and ID-DEP-C6, carries a MUST-present completeness rule with a fixed threshold, has its own corpus change class, and is REFUSE-only when absent. The ambiguity enum encodes the conflict-refuse outcome it could not express. G16-13 makes the selectorDecisionDigest join a failed successor when omitted. The Codex v4 advisory is recorded and credited, all four governing sources are re-verified in one block at the adopted HEAD, and the corpus domain is now the manifest-declared dependent product, which is better aligned with the live DR-G16 constraint cell than the formulation it replaces. Fourteen measurements pass and there is no blocker - the first time in this chain. What stops acceptance is bookkeeping in one small area. Two paths inside /reMeasurementAtV5 were edited off-roster, dropping the enumeration convention v5 introduced as its own repair; and three clauses - including the governing-source role for COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md itself - still name reMeasurementAtV5 as the live pin while the same artifact stamps that block HISTORICAL-AT-V5, with the honesty entry reporting the advisory discharged on the strength of the one locator that was fixed. No pin is wrong in fact; every digest verifies live. DR-121 remains OPEN; DR-G16 remains PROPOSED, not QUALIFIED.
authorityOfThisVerdict: This verdict is a reviewer opinion recorded for coordinator disposition. It applies nothing, edits no subject, marks no row SATISFIED, marks no gate QUALIFIED, authorizes no implementation, chooses no CI vendor, mints no D-096 (A) grant, and does not touch docs/v2/architecture/08-decision-and-readiness-register.md or docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md.
coordinatorNote: A v7 needs a very small roster: /recordedInputs/governingSources/3/role, /reMeasurementAtV3, /reMeasurementAtV4, /reMeasurementAtV5, and /honestyRepairsFromV5 - all bookkeeping, no design work. If the standing-field restructure suggested at V6-S2 is adopted in the same pass, this family should not appear again, and the roster for v8 and beyond would not need to grow with each generation. Worth recording for disposition: the substantive contract has been stable across two cycles now - v6 changed no selector rule, no lane universe rule, no evidence rule and no acceptance class except to strengthen the three the reviews asked for - so the remaining distance to a zero-zero candidate is bookkeeping only. Two process notes. First, keeping frozen predecessor verdicts readable while barring the concurrent reviewer worked again: it is what let this verdict certify both Codex characterizations instead of recording them as uncertifiable, and it is worth stating explicitly in future prompts. Second, this reviewer accepted v5's cartesian coverageLaw at M-11 of the v5 verdict and Codex was right to challenge it as MCICV5-S2; v6's dependent product is the better rule and the correction is recorded here.
